description: Figure 8(d) presents a line plot titled “The performance on Qwen2.5,” illustrating the post-edit probing accuracy (ACC (%)) for five different knowledge editing methods—Base, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000), with tick marks at intervals of 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 80% with tick marks at 5% intervals. The plot contains five data series, each represented by a distinct line and marker: Base (black solid line with circles), FT (blue solid line with triangles), MEMIT (purple solid line with diamonds), IKE (red solid line with triangles), and ROME (green solid line with squares). All lines show an increasing trend as the co-occurrence number increases, starting at approximately 60% to 65% for the Base model and rising to around 75% to 80% for the ROME model. The ROME line consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while the Base line remains the lowest. No data is plotted for the Qwen2.5 model, as the plot area is entirely grayed out.
